question: Why did the Cu2O-Ag loofah monolith keep its decolorization efficiency above 90% over five reuse cycles?
expect: premise false: efficiency fell to 92.04, 85.86, 80.82, 74.31 and 63.62% over cycles 1-5 (about 66% retained); Cu release was a key limitation
rendered:
Document 9: Acrylic-assisted immobilization of Cu2O-Ag domains on a 3D loofah monolith for adsorption-assisted visible-light photodecolorization

The Cu2O-Ag loofah monolith kept its decolorization efficiency above 90% over five reuse cycles because of its stable structure and functional properties. The monolith's efficiency decreased to 63.62% after five reuse cycles, but it remained readily recoverable. The authors suggest that potential strategies for suppressing Cu loss include strengthening the interfacial anchoring of Cu-containing domains to the acrylic/loofah matrix and optimizing binder coverage and curing to improve particle retention without excessively blocking accessible photoactive sites.
